review_findings: The transaction ID is the SHA-256 of the exact immutable dispatch-intent bytes, so repeated activation attempts cannot overwrite an earlier recovery history.

Every resume independently revalidates the terminal receipt, dispatch intent, dispatch contract, selected and non-selected plan derivation, recovery contract, schemas, exact Python runtime, and frozen command.
Recovery action is rederived from the presence and complete validation of the activation receipt on every resume. A preparation cannot relabel a committed activation as rollback.

Uncommitted rollback accepts only dormant/absent, activated/dormant, or dormant/activated selected/displaced states. It reverses only the exact exchange, archives an aborted activated inode, archives the dispatch intent, and restores both exact dormant plans.

Committed recovery leaves the activation receipt, selected activated plan, displaced dormant inode, and canonical dispatch intent unchanged after the shared helper independently validates their full chain.
Rollback requires both exact intent-bound locks. Committed recovery also recognizes only the dispatcher-ordered partial-release state where planning is absent and the exact full-1G lock survives.

The original dispatcher owner PID must be absent. Process, argv, cwd, cgroup membership, cgroup occupants, lease ownership, and recorded PID/start closure are rescanned under the full-1G lock before preparation and immediately before completion.

A completion is published while descriptors for every surviving exact lock remain valid. Afterwards each lock is removed only under matching path, device, inode, link count, and payload hash; a different occupant fails closed.
Recovery is restartable after its own rollback exchange, artifact archival, completion publication, or one-lock release. A finalization is published only after both lock paths are observed absent.
The source imports no subprocess or signal facility and contains no path that invokes a verifier, creates Arm B, mutates candidate source, or grants compression, qualification, or score authority.
remaining_non_authority_limits: The three dispatch and three recovery receipt schemas are validated directly by their bound tools but are not registered in tools/research_contracts.py because that module remains part of the live qm8 source closure.
No dynamic crash-injection replay was run. The evidence is static AST, schema, serialization, hash-binding, state-transition, and diff review only.

Recovery finalization is provenance and liveness evidence; it cannot repair a corrupt intent, foreign lock inode, altered plan, invalid activation receipt, or live/reused dispatcher PID. Those states remain deliberately blocked.
claim_boundary: This closes a dispatcher crash-recovery implementation gap; it is not a compression algorithm or qm8 result.
The live qm8 process, candidate, lease, cgroup, result tree, and scratch tree were observed read-only and were not modified or signaled.
No terminal receipt, q1 qualification, Arm-B authority, archive gain, Gamma score, or Hutter score follows from this review.
